title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: MCP-based agents for US Government clouds
summary: Hold: the licensing field says Microsoft has not published an entitlement, although the cited prerequisites document general agent entitlements and include custom actions in their licensing table. The roadmap facts, blocking controls and reported disagreements about government-cloud availability are supported.

claims.claim: The roadmap introduces MCP-based agent support in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: We’re introducing support for Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot .

claims.claim: The roadmap says developers can build Copilot agents using MCP servers.
claims.quote: This update enables developers to build Copilot agents using MCP servers

claims.claim: The roadmap says users interact with these agents through familiar experiences.
claims.quote: allows users to interact with these agents using familiar experiences.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for this government-cloud MCP enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP agents GCC GCC High DoD licensing default rollout 564607; "564607" rollout default MCP. Read the record, MCP walkthrough, prerequisites, known issues and agent management; none states this item's arrival default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has not published which entitlement covers these MCP-based agents.
claims.quote: | Custom actions | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to "included". Replace the licensing notes and the Licence paragraph with: "Learn's general agent licensing table includes custom actions in Copilot Chat without usage-based billing and in licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot. Government-cloud support remains subject to the conflicting availability statements described above; MCP-specific government licensing terms are not separately published." In Open questions, replace the licence-or-meter question with "Are there any MCP-specific government licensing terms beyond the general agent entitlements?" In the cost rationale, replace "the licence for MCP-based agents in US Government clouds is not yet published" with "Learn documents general agent entitlements but no separate MCP-specific government licensing terms". The cited prerequisites table expressly covers custom actions, the class that includes MCP plugins.

claims.claim: The sources do not publish separate MCP-specific government-cloud licensing terms.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP government GCC license custom actions included licensing; "MCP" "GCC" "license". Opened prerequisites, the Copilot licensing page and service description; general entitlements are documented, not separate MCP government terms.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: MCP plugins are custom actions within declarative agents.
claims.quote: MCP and API plugins are custom actions that enable declarative agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot to interact with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The plugin manifest connects an agent to a remote MCP server without packaging or hosting the running server.
claims.quote: The plugin manifest connects the agent to a remote MCP server; it doesn't package or host the running server.

claims.claim: Copilot dynamically resolves declarative-agent MCP plugin tools from the server at runtime by default.
claims.quote: For plugins based on an MCP server, Copilot resolves the plugin's tools dynamically at runtime by default, directly from the MCP server.

claims.claim: A developer can instead pin a fixed tool set in the plugin manifest.
claims.quote: When building the agent, a developer can optionally pin a fixed set of tools in the plugin manifest instead.

claims.claim: The Copilot service description lists declarative agents as not currently available in DoD.
claims.quote: | Declarative agents | Yes | Yes | Yes^8^ | Not currently available |

claims.claim: The service description limits GCC High declarative agents to Agent Builder creations and those published via admin controls.
claims.quote: GCC-High currently only supports declarative agents created using Agent Builder and those published via admin controls.

claims.claim: The declarative-agent overview instead lists limited DoD support for pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.
claims.quote: Department of Defense (DoD): Limited support - only pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit are supported. Agent Builder isn't available for declarative agents in DoD.

claims.claim: The declarative-agent overview supports both Toolkit pro-code agents and Agent Builder in GCCH.
claims.quote: Government Community Cloud High (GCCH): Pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit are supported. Agent Builder is also now available in GCCH.

claims.quote: The following features aren't currently supported in Microsoft 365 Government tenants: ... Authenticated custom actions.

claims.claim: Known issues lists usage billing for extensibility features as unsupported in Government tenants.
claims.quote: The following features aren't currently supported in Microsoft 365 Government tenants: ... Support for usage billing for extensibility features.

claims.quote: The following features aren't currently supported in Microsoft 365 Government tenants: ... Support for publishing agents via the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

claims.claim: Learn does not provide a government-cloud-specific description of this roadmap item's MCP enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP agents GCC GCC High DoD licensing default rollout 564607; "564607" rollout default MCP. Opened the MCP overview, walkthrough, declarative-agent overview, service description and known issues; found general guidance, not an item-specific explanation.

claims.claim: An agent's MCP tool access is subject to authentication, permissions and its tool configuration.
claims.quote: A plugin doesn't grant a user access to data that the user or component isn't otherwise authorized to access.

claims.claim: The sources do not state that this enablement changes existing behaviour for other users.
claims.quote: Searched: "564607" rollout default MCP; Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP government default enabled rollout tenant switch allowlist. Read the record, MCP overview, walkthrough and agent management; none announces a change to existing users' behaviour for this item.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The agent sends MCP requests to a separately hosted server outside Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: The agent sends a request to the plugin's MCP server or API, which is hosted outside of Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Learn does not specify the relationship of this feature's remote MCP server to government cloud boundaries.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP government data boundary hosting GCC DoD. Read MCP overview, walkthrough and Plan data, privacy, and security; reviewed government overview search excerpts. General external-service responsibilities do not specify this feature's government boundary.

claims.claim: Prerequisites says agents grounded in shared tenant work data are unavailable in GCC, GCCH and DoD.
claims.quote: Agents grounded in shared tenant work data aren't currently available in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud (GCC), Government Community Cloud High (GCCH), or Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: The walkthrough's OAuth registration lets Copilot obtain an access token on behalf of the signed-in user for each MCP call.
claims.quote: Copilot then uses the registration to obtain an access token on behalf of the signed-in user each time the agent calls the MCP server.

claims.claim: The MCP apps page permits authentication type None for an unauthenticated development server.
claims.quote: If your MCP server is still in development and doesn't implement authentication, select None as the authentication type.

claims.claim: The MCP apps page says to add authentication before production deployment.
claims.quote: Add authentication before you deploy to production.

claims.claim: Learn's Government restriction on authenticated custom actions includes authenticated MCP actions.
claims.quote: The following features aren't currently supported in Microsoft 365 Government tenants: ... Authenticated custom actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: MCP and API plugins can create, update and delete connected-system data when supported.
claims.quote: users can ask a declarative agent to query an MCP server or REST API for information and, when supported, create, update, and delete data and objects through natural language prompts.

claims.claim: Dynamic discovery can obtain a changed tool set without repackaging or republishing the agent.
claims.quote: Dynamic tool discovery means you get the latest tools the MCP server exposes without waiting for the agent to be repackaged and republished.

claims.claim: Prerequisites describes agent licensing through a Copilot add-on, Copilot Business, Microsoft 365 E7 and usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license ... Microsoft 365 Copilot Business ... Microsoft 365 E7 (Frontier Suite) ... Usage-based billing (pay-as-you-go)

claims.claim: Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences have access to enhanced agent capabilities.
claims.quote: users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses have access to agents with enhanced capabilities, such as grounding with SharePoint data and Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors.

claims.claim: Users in tenants with usage-based billing enabled can access enhanced agent capabilities.
claims.quote: Users in tenants that have Copilot Studio pay-as-you-go billing enabled (consumed as Copilot Credits) and users with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses have access to agents with enhanced capabilities

claims.claim: Agent usage-based billing is measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing (pay-as-you-go) - Tenants can enable agent access without a full license, with some limitations to agent configuration options. Consumption is measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Prerequisites says usage-based billing is unsupported in GCCH and GCC.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing isn't supported in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud High (GCCH) and Government Community Cloud (GCC) environments.

claims.claim: The prerequisites page's usage-billing statement does not name DoD.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP agents GCC GCC High DoD licensing default rollout 564607. Opened and read prerequisites in full: the billing exclusion names GCC and GCCH; DoD appears in the separate shared-tenant-work-data exclusion, not in the billing statement.

claims.claim: The MCP walkthrough requires the Copilot extensibility prerequisites.
claims.quote: Before you begin, make sure that you have the following prerequisites: ... Requirements specified in Requirements for Copilot extensibility options

claims.claim: Toolkit developers need their administrator to enable sideloading custom apps.
claims.quote: To build agents with Agents Toolkit and other IDEs, you must have your admin enable the ability to sideload a custom app to your tenant.

claims.claim: Learn's management guidance says organisation publishing is supported in GCCH and GCCM.
claims.quote: Publishing agents to the organization is supported in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud High (GCCH) and Government Community Cloud Moderate (GCCM) environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated rollout mechanics specific to this roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP agents GCC GCC High DoD licensing default rollout 564607; "564607" rollout default MCP. Read the record, MCP walkthrough, prerequisites, known issues and management guidance; no item-specific rollout procedure was found.

claims.claim: Agents published by the organisation go through admin approval.
claims.quote: Before you make these agents available to members of your organization, these agents go through an admin approval to ensure compliance and readiness.

claims.claim: Agent inventory can be reviewed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block > Block agent > Save blocks the selected agent across the organisation.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... select an agent ... select Block or Unblock. ... select either Block agent or Unblock agent, and then select Save.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The block API is a preview Microsoft Graph beta operation.
claims.quote: | Block (preview) | POST `/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block` | Block a package to prevent its usage. |

claims.claim: Agent blocking targets the selected agent and does not necessarily block shared MCP servers or revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.
